### Choosing Coffee Beans

Arabica beans produce sweeter, more complex flavour than Robusta. Light roasts are acidic and fruity; dark roasts are richer and bittersweet.

### Grind Size and Extraction

Finer grinds increase surface area for faster extraction and suit espresso. Coarser grinds slow extraction and work best for French press and cold brew.

### Water Temperature

Ideal brewing temperature is 90–96 °C. Water below 85 °C yields sour, under-extracted coffee; above 96 °C causes bitterness.

### Brew Time

Espresso extracts in 25–30 seconds. French press steeps for 4 minutes. Pour-over takes 3–4 minutes. Longer steeping generally increases body and bitterness.

### Coffee-to-Water Ratio

A standard ratio is 1:15 to 1:17 by weight. Adjusting this ratio is the most direct way to control brew strength without changing grind or temperature.
